sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.content: India's artificial intelligence market is valued at approximately Rs 1.2 to 1.5 lakh crore in 2026 [E1], with an annual growth rate of 28% to 35% [E2]. The country accounts for approximately 5% to 6% of the global artificial intelligence market [E3] and has recorded significant funding and startup activity [E4][E5]. However, the market faces major challenges, including a severe skills gap (verify the current status) [E6] and an evolving regulatory landscape [E7][E8].

sections.title: Market Insights
sections.content: The artificial intelligence market in India is valued at approximately Rs 1.2 to 1.5 lakh crore in 2026 [E1] and grows at an annual rate of 28% to 35% [E2]. India accounts for approximately 5% to 6% of the global artificial intelligence market [E3]. Indian artificial intelligence startups raised over $3 billion (United States dollars) in 2023 to 2024 [E5], and the country recorded $1.22 billion in artificial intelligence specific funding in 2025 [E4]. Total data center capacity in India exceeded 700MW (megawatts) by 2024 [E9], and India is expected to attract $200 billion in data centre investment by 2030 [E10]. The semiconductor market in India may reach $100 billion to $110 billion by 2030 [E11]. Demand for artificial intelligence skills is driven heavily by the technology and BFSI (Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance) sectors [E12]. At the same time, workforce constraints are significant, as nearly 45% of Indian organisations identify artificial intelligence, digital, and data skills as their single largest workforce constraint [E13]. There is an 82.9% generative artificial intelligence skills gap in India [E6], and only 25% of Indian organisations believe their workforce is adequately prepared to use artificial intelligence effectively [E14]. Furthermore, India could face a shortage of more than 1.4 million artificial intelligence professionals by 2026 [E15], with 300,000 to 400,000 unfilled positions [E16].

sections.title: Competitor Analysis
sections.content: The accepted evidence does not identify enough verified companies providing products or services in the Artificial Intelligence market to support a company-level competitor comparison. Funding and investor activity may provide market context, but do not establish that an organisation is a competitor.

sections.title: Opportunities and Risks
sections.content:
Opportunities:
• Significant capital is flowing into the sector, with investors committing over 250 billion dollars at the 2026 India AI Impact Summit to support infrastructure and research [E17].
• India is positioned to become a major hub for data center infrastructure, with expectations to attract 200 billion dollars in investment by 2030 [E10].
• The semiconductor market in India presents a substantial growth opportunity, projected to reach between 100 billion and 110 billion dollars by 2030 [E11].
Risks:
• There is a severe shortage of qualified professionals, with projections indicating a potential deficit of more than 1.4 million AI experts by 2026 [E15].
• The medical sector faces specific ethical and legal risks regarding AI, particularly concerning patient consent, the secondary use of data, and data repurposing [E18].
• Existing legal frameworks, such as the Information Technology (IT) Act, currently lack specific provisions to address the unique challenges posed by artificial intelligence (verify the current status) [E19].

sections.title: Recommendations
sections.content:
• Invest in targeted training and upskilling programs to help mitigate the reported 82.9% generative artificial intelligence skills gap [E6] and the shortage of professionals [E15].
• Monitor regulatory developments closely, including the India AI Governance Guidelines (verify the current status) [E7] and the Artificial Intelligence (Ethics & Accountability) Bill [E8], to ensure compliance with emerging rules.
• Evaluate data management practices against the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (verify the current status) [E20] to address legal risks related to data consent and repurposing [E18].

sections.title: Glossary
sections.content:
Simple explanations of important terms used in this report. These definitions are explanatory notes, not research evidence.
- BFSI: Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance is an industry grouping representing financial institutions.
- Semiconductor: Semiconductors are essential materials used to manufacture computer chips and electronic hardware.
- Generative Artificial Intelligence: Generative artificial intelligence refers to systems capable of creating new content such as text, images, or code.
- Data Center: A data center is a specialized facility that houses computer systems and associated infrastructure for storing and processing data.
- Upskilling: Upskilling is the process of teaching employees new skills to improve their job performance.
